Proving Grounds — stage review

58 proposed stages, 3×5 → 10×10. Terrain only — armies are generator output dealt onto each stage (royal rearmost row, pawns in front; the deal AUTO-CROPS rows behind either king, so kings always start on the extreme rows — sample captions say when that fired). Dark squares are stone (a boundary); ▦ on the wood tint is FURNITURE (§4.6) — a neutral capturable occupant either side may smash by capturing onto it. Deleting every ▦ must still leave a sensible arena (the stone-only corpus control arm). For each stage: keep / tweak / kill — call tweaks by coordinates (one char per square in the JSON: '.' floor, '#' stone, '^' furniture). Samples are seeded and reproducible; "not shown" means the generator rejected every attempt (that is data too). Balance testing runs every stage in BOTH vertical orientations (designer rule — mirrors are not separate scenarios), so judge terrain on its own merits, not by which side it faces.

Wave 5 — locked (rooms & breaches + the s51+ floorplans — all 25 accepted 2026-08-26)

Double Doors s34-double-doors

8×9 · 6 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

The requested archetype, plain: one full wall, one ^^ double door, no other way through. Furniture alone joins the halves — the verifier flags it; you smash in.

The Antechamber s35-the-antechamber

7×10 · 11 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Two partitions in sequence: an open door into the antechamber, then a ^^ double door into the far hall. Room-corridor-room the way a generator would draw it.

Crate Hoard s36-crate-hoard

8×8 · 7 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A holed corner room with the hoard inside — and now a breakable floor-edge (c5, d5) so the room can be cracked open from below as well as entered through the gap. Designer tweak 2026-08-26.

Twin Vaults s37-twin-vaults

10×8 · 4 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A full-height spine splits the field into two vaults — one open hole, one weak point — with a crate cluster stored in each half. Two sub-battles, three ways to merge them.

Quartered s38-quartered

9×9 · 11 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A cross of walls cuts the board into four rooms. Two passages are open holes, two are weak points — the generator's room-graph made literal.

The Vestibule s39-the-vestibule

8×10 · 8 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A sealed central chamber with ^^ double doors facing BOTH armies. Take the flanks around it, or smash into the middle and hold the room.

Broken Cloister s40-broken-cloister

9×9 · 9 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A solid garden block with clutter heaped at its four bends — the ring corridor narrows to single files exactly where the crates sit.

Supply Line s41-supply-line

10×7 · 8 walls · 6 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A full wall with one ^^ double door, and supply crates stacked AGAINST the wall on both sides. Furniture integrated into the wall structure; the door is the only way through.

Guardroom s42-guardroom

10×7 · 4 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Three rooms in a row. One door is open, one is weak — and the weak one has a crate shoved behind it as a barricade. Wide-shallow room-graph with clean deployment rows.

The Breach s43-the-breach

8×9 · 13 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A castle wall two ranks thick. The breach column is rubble-choked — and the collapse spilled forward: d5 joins the breach and d6 lies in the approach. Smash a path, or smash a wider one. Designer tweak 2026-08-26.

Double Gatehouse s44-double-gatehouse

10×9 · 6 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

One wall, TWO ^^ double doors at the thirds, nothing open. Pick a gate — or price both and let the engine tell you which.

Collapsed Arch s45-collapsed-arch

7×8 · 3 walls · 3 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A wall whose arch came down: a 3-wide rubble cluster IN the wall itself, plus one intact slip at the edge. Clear the rubble for the broad front or file through the slip.

Cellar Steps s46-cellar-steps

6×8 · 3 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A tiny sealed cellar in the near corner — stone on two sides, a weak ceiling slab, a crate on the stairs. Molding can put your own pieces inside; someone has to dig them out.

The Warrens s47-the-warrens

9×10 · 15 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Two full walls and an offset divider, now multiply breached: two weak points per wall and a breakable stub on the divider — every route is a smash, and there are many routes. Verifier-flagged. Designer tweak 2026-08-26.

Barricaded Bridge s48-barricaded-bridge

7×7 · 4 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Stone flanks force everything over a center bridge, and the bridge is half-blocked by a two-crate barricade. One open file under fire, or clear the barricade.

Crate Quarry s49-crate-quarry

9×7 · 0 walls · 9 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Clusters only, no stone: a 2x2 block, a 1x3 run, a 2x1 pair. The pure-cluster control — its stone-only arm is an empty field.

Last Stand s50-last-stand

8×9 · 6 walls · 3 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

The redoubt evolved: a far-side pocket with a ^^ double door AND a crate shoring it from inside — three smashes through the center, or come around the flank files.

The Corridor s51-the-corridor

10×10 · 20 walls · 10 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: a full-width hallway with two rooms off each side — five areas. Each wall has an open door and a weak door; the room pairs also connect to each other through breakable party doors (e8, f1). NW stocks a crate pair, NE one against the wall, SE an L of three, SW stands bare.

The Apartments s52-the-apartments

10×10 · 17 walls · 12 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: three rooms upstairs, two down, six doors — every room reachable two ways, party doors between neighbours (d7, g8, e2). Furnishings differ room to room: a wardrobe pair, a lone chest, a corner stack, a bare parlor.

The Cellblock s53-the-cellblock

10×9 · 24 walls · 8 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: a central hallway with three cells off each side — seven areas. Left doors are all breakable; right doors alternate open and weak. Some cells hold contraband, some are swept bare.

Banquet & Kitchens s54-banquet-and-kitchens

10×10 · 11 walls · 11 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: a great hall dominated by a four-crate banquet table, and three kitchens behind a wall with a double door and a weak service hatch. The kitchens connect to each other (d7 breakable, g7 open), each stocked differently.

Gate & Bailey s55-gate-and-bailey

10×10 · 17 walls · 6 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: an outer wall with a double gate and an open postern, a bailey with stabled crates along the west wall, and a stone keep with one weak door — which the defender may mold inside. Three zones deep.

The Archive s56-the-archive

9×10 · 9 walls · 15 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: two long shelf-rows make three aisles in the stacks; the reading room behind the double door is the only way to the far side (verifier-flagged smash-in), and an inner cage with its own weak door guards the rarest holdings.

Crossroads Market s57-crossroads-market

10×9 · 16 walls · 10 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: two hallways cross at an open square, with an L-walled stall in each quadrant — five areas, every stall door different (two weak, two placements), every stall stocked differently: one chest, a pair, a spill of three, one empty.

Drowned Halls s58-drowned-halls

10×10 · 20 walls · 9 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

FLOORPLAN: the dense one — six areas. Two full walls with mixed doors bracket a mid band split into three chambers by dividers with party doors (d4, g5); the north territory splits again behind a weak door. Flooded chambers hold flotsam; the center hall is scoured bare.

Wave 4 — locked (the furniture bed — all 33 accepted 2026-08-26; replaced the retired waves 1–3)

Bare Cell s01-bare-cell

3×5 · 0 walls · 0 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 3×2

The minimum board, zero terrain — the pure-duel control and the smallest arena the trigger can draw. Deliberately untouched by furniture.

Cluttered Closet s02-cluttered-closet

3×6 · 0 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 3×2

Smallest crate fight: two pieces of furniture on otherwise open minimum-width ground. Every capture-the-clutter line is worth a tempo question even at 3 files.

The Pantry s03-the-pantry

4×6 · 1 walls · 3 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 4×2

Small mixed ground: one stone pillar among shelves of clutter, packed toward midfield so both armies still deploy. First taste of stone-vs-furniture reading at a glance.

Barrel Row s04-barrel-row

5×7 · 0 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 7×2

A broken furniture line across midfield, no stone at all. The stone-only control arm of this stage is an open field — the crates ARE the terrain.

The Squeeze s05-the-squeeze

5×8 · 4 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 7×2

Stone waist leaving a 2-wide pass, with one crate narrowing it further — pay a capture to widen the pass, or file through under fire.

Crate Court s06-crate-court

6×8 · 2 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Pillared court with loose clutter: two stone pillars, four crates. Baseline mixed-density middle-size arena.

The Doorway s07-the-doorway

6×9 · 4 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A full wall with a 2-wide door — one leaf open, one leaf furniture. Smash the door for the wide file or funnel through the open half.

Storeroom s08-storeroom

6×7 · 0 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

One-sided clutter: five crates crowd one deployment approach, the other is clean. Asymmetric by design — the flip convention tests it facing each side.

Long Gallery s09-long-gallery

4×10 · 3 walls · 0 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 7×2

Narrow-tall pure-stone gallery, staggered pillars. The stone-only reference point among the tall boards — no furniture on purpose.

Broken Barricade s10-broken-barricade

8×10 · 2 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A furniture barricade spanning the field between stone end-stubs, one open gap. Fight for the gap or smash a second one — the engine prices both.

Grand Hall s11-grand-hall

10×10 · 3 walls · 5 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

The big open hall: three stone pillars, five scattered furnishings. Light terrain at maximum size — long diagonals still live here.

Rat Nest s12-rat-nest

10×8 · 6 walls · 7 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Density stress: dense mixed pockets of stone and clutter, including one crate in each deployment approach. The generator must still deal every army width here.

Gatehouse s13-gatehouse

6×8 · 4 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 7×2

Stone stubs in BOTH back ranks with a furniture gate-leaf beside each. Crates on the king rows are capture-promotion squares (§4.6) — march a pawn and smash in.

Weak Wall s14-weak-wall

8×8 · 6 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A full-width stone wall whose only ways through are two furniture breaches. Furniture alone separates the armies — legal (§4.6), the verifier flags it: you MUST smash in.

Colonnade s15-colonnade

7×9 · 4 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Pillar pairs with furniture stacked between them — the colonnade reads solid until somebody starts clearing the shelving.

Cave Mouth s16-cave-mouth

5×7 · 3 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 5×2

The near back rank is rock except a 1-square mouth and a weak-masonry plug. The king molds into the mouth; the enemy can capture-promote onto the plug.

Rubble Yard s17-rubble-yard

9×8 · 4 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Mixed stone-and-crate rubble strictly in midfield, deployment rows clean. The workhorse mixed-density case for the corpus.

Split Cellars s18-split-cellars

10×8 · 4 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Stone spurs split both deployment areas into cellar pockets; crates sit where a door would be. Molding pours armies around the spurs.

Diagonal Scar s19-diagonal-scar

8×9 · 4 walls · 3 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A broken diagonal alternating stone and furniture. The scar can be partially reopened — every second segment is smashable.

The Anvil s20-the-anvil

4×9 · 2 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 7×2

Mirrored materials: stone pair on one side's second rank, crate pair on the other's. Same shape, different permanence — the cleanest A/B of wall vs furniture in deployment.

Collapsed Keep s21-collapsed-keep

10×10 · 10 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Big-board stress: rubble in both deployment zones, room walls midfield, loose crates in the wreckage. The 10x10 everything-at-once case.

Sinkhole s22-sinkhole

6×7 · 4 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A 2x2 stone sink with furniture heaped on its flanks — the hole is forever, the heap is not.

The Neck s23-the-neck

7×9 · 10 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Room-corridor-room with offset throats sharing one furniture column. The only stone-open cells are NOT adjacent — clearing the crate column is the fast route. Verifier-flagged smash-in (§4.6).

Hypostyle s24-hypostyle

9×8 · 4 walls · 4 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Alternating pillar lattice — half the pillars are stone, half furniture. The lattice thins as the duel burns through it.

The Divide s25-the-divide

8×9 · 9 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A full central spine with two corridors — except one spine cell is furniture. Route A: the corridor. Route B: make your own door.

Flats s26-flats

10×6 · 0 walls · 3 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

Wide-shallow ground with only light clutter and no stone. Wide flanks, short files — the cavalry board.

Posterngate s27-posterngate

6×8 · 8 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 6×2

Both back ranks walled except opposite-corner gates — one leaf open, one furniture. Kings mold into the gates; the auto-crop and camp lines earn their keep here.

Parapet s28-parapet

7×8 · 5 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

The near second rank is a parapet with one open slot and one weak slot — pawns deploy DEEP, and the camp line sits forward of the king row.

The Redoubt s29-the-redoubt

8×8 · 4 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A sealed corner chamber in the far side's territory whose only door is furniture. Sometimes the defender molds INTO it — a fortress with a capturable door is the §4.6 thesis stage.

The Serpent s30-the-serpent

5×10 · 11 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

S-weave of stone arms with crates at two bends. The long way is safe; the short way is bought with captures.

Ruined L s31-ruined-l

9×9 · 14 walls · 2 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 8×2

A solid collapsed quadrant makes an L-shaped playfield; two weak-masonry cells on the ruin's edge can be dug out for nooks.

Smugglers' Hold s32-smugglers-hold

3×7 · 4 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 3×2

Three-wide staggered passes, one plugged with contraband. Knife-fight geometry at minimum width.

The Vault s33-the-vault

5×5 · 1 walls · 1 furniture · largest mirror army that fits: 5×2

The minimum square: one crate, one pillar, gap 1. The smallest board where stone and furniture coexist.
